newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - British Telecom rises.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - British Telecom rises.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc rose Wednesday on reports of a possible alliance with Spain's Telefonica de Espana, highlighting quiet trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

Traders reported mostly low volumes after the U.S. Consumer Price Index for February was slightly stronger than expected, fueling speculation that the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) would raise interest rates at its meeting next week.
ADRs were "terribly quiet here," a trader said. "Volumes are very thin. I think all eyes are on the FOMC meeting."

British Telecom rose 3-1/8 to 73-3/4 on a report in Britain's Financial Times newspaper that the company was negotiating a stake in Telefonica de Espana's international unit, which has holdings in South American countries that include Argentina, Chile and Peru.
Telefonica de Espana rose one to 71. Neither company would comment on the report, and volume in both ADRs was low.

Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd fell 3/16 to 53-3/4 in moderate trade after it denied reports that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had ordered changes in the labeling of the company's Copaxone drug.
Lehman Brothers reiterated a buy rating on Teva, saying a recent selloff was unwarranted.
